comparison: Both strongly support the diaphragm EMG findings (C18-C28) and experimental design (C2-C3). OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation while peer reviewers emphasize the convincing nature of the data. Peer review R1 also includes C29-C31 (wild-type vs ChAT-Cre comparison) which OpenEval addresses separately in R2.

OpenEval R2 focuses specifically on the wild-type vs ChAT-Cre comparison (C29-C31), finding it well-supported with appropriate statistics. Peer R1 includes these claims as part of a broader evaluation and identifies this comparison as a key strength of the study.

Both address survival data (C32-C34). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to marginal p-value (0.069), small sample size, and unclear mortality cause. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED without raising concerns, suggesting implicit acceptance of the authors' reporting despite the statistical uncertainty.

Perfect agreement on control experiments (C35-C36). Both find the negative controls validate DREADD-ligand specificity. OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification while peer reviewers implicitly accept these controls as part of rigorous experimental design.

Both support ventilation findings (C38-C40) in awake rats. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis and notes consistency of results. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the ventilation measurements as convincing and rigorous, identifying them as a study strength.

Both address phrenic nerve recordings. OpenEval R6 covers comprehensive phrenic data (C41-C49) including blood pressure effects, rating all as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 focuses on core phrenic findings (C7, C37, C42-C44) with strong endorsement of rigor and convincing data.

Both address cardiovascular effects (C45-C49). OpenEval explicitly notes blood pressure decrease as a notable side effect requiring consideration for clinical translation. Peer reviewers do not question these findings, suggesting implicit acceptance without specific concern.

Divergent evaluations of C41 (time post-injection effects). OpenEval finds the lack of relationship between timing and response supports stable DREADD expression (SUPPORTED). Peer R8 rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 specifically questioning whether variable post-infection timing was adequately considered in comparisons.

Strong agreement on histological validation (C50-C53). OpenEval finds expression patterns correlate well with physiological responses. Peer reviewers specifically praise rigorous assessment of DREADD expression. OpenEval also addresses C68 (lack of retrograde labeling) which peer R6 includes.

Perfect agreement on main conclusions (C54, C70-C71). Both strongly support that DREADDs can drive phrenic activity and that targeted expression is superior. OpenEval provides detailed justification from experimental data while peer reviewers explicitly endorse the convincing nature and importance of findings.

Complete agreement on methodological limitations (C67, C72). Both accept the authors' acknowledgment of expression variability and need for improved delivery methods. OpenEval views this as appropriate scientific self-critique; peer reviewers implicitly accept without challenge.

Perfect agreement on negative pilot data (C81-C82). Both support the transparent reporting of unsuccessful delivery methods and predictions for optimization. OpenEval notes this represents appropriate reporting of negative results; peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of methodological development.

Both address translational potential (C55, C73-C74) but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative and require substantial additional work including addressing safety concerns. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing translational potential as 'important first step' toward clinical applications.

OpenEval R10 addresses mechanistic interpretations (C57-C60, C62-C66) regarding DREADD function, feedback mechanisms, and differences between phrenic nerve and EMG responses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly comment on these mechanistic claims.

OpenEval R13 evaluates background literature and rationale (C1, C8-C17) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly assess the background claims or literature citations.

Both address lack of retrograde labeling (C68-C69). OpenEval finds the convergent evidence (anatomy, histology, function) adequately supports conclusions despite this limitation. Peer R6 includes C68 in their histological assessment but does not specifically critique the absence of retrograde confirmation.

OpenEval R15 evaluates literature context and novelty claims (C75-C90) as SUPPORTED, finding the claim of novelty justified given prior work focused on hypoglossal rather than phrenic motoneurons. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
